events.title: Eastern Market — Weekend Market & Flea

events.title: Garfield Park

events.title: National Mall & Smithsonian Museums

events.title: Anacostia Riverwalk Trail Ride
events.description: Paved riverfront trail for a family bike ride, with Capital Bikeshare access nearby.

events.title: The Fields at RFK — Community Open Play & Disc Golf
events.time: Open hours vary (8 AM–dusk disc golf)
events.venue: The Fields at RFK Campus (401 Oklahoma Ave NE)
events.description: Turf fields with community open-play hours plus DC's free disc golf course. 10-min walk from Stadium-Armory.

events.title: CHAW Gallery (Capitol Hill Arts Workshop)
events.venue: Capitol Hill Arts Workshop (545 7th St SE)
events.description: Rotating gallery shows of local artists, two blocks from Eastern Market. Check site for current exhibition.

events.title: Improvapalooza 2026 – Washington Improv Theater
events.venue: Washington Improv Theater at Studio Theatre
events.price: Nightly passes $25 (+$2.47 service fee); All-Palooza Pass $80
events.description: WIT's community-beloved marathon of experimental improv comedy — more than 200 shows over five days. Expect outlandish costumes, big ideas, and big laughs. Each show is completely different. Festival-style, first-come seating. Runs Wed Aug 19 through Mon Aug 24, overlapping the Aug 22–23 weekend.

events.title: Eastern Market Main Street – Free Friday Jazz Under the Shed (August Fridays)
events.venue: Eastern Market Farmer's Line Shed, 225 7th St SE
events.description: Every Friday evening in August, relax under the shade of the Eastern Market farmer's line shed for free live jazz. Sponsored by Jason Secrest / Coldwell Banker. August 7 featured Amy K. Bormet; subsequent Fridays (Aug 14, 21, 28) continue the series.

events.title: DC Summer Restaurant Week
events.description: Washington DC's biannual Restaurant Week returns with hundreds of restaurants offering special prix-fixe menus at $25, $35, and $55 price points — a great opportunity to try the city's top dining destinations.

events.title: The Notebook
events.price: From ~$57 (resale avg ~$210); TodayTix rush/lottery may apply
events.description: The Broadway touring production of The Notebook, based on the best-selling novel and iconic film. Plays the weekends of Aug 22–23 and Aug 29–30.

events.title: The Notebook – Broadway at the National
events.venue: The National Theatre, 1321 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.description: Inspired by the best-selling book and classic film, this Broadway musical adaptation of The Notebook plays at the National Theatre. Broadway at the National rounds out its summer lineup with this unforgettable take on the iconic love story.

events.title: DC Public Library – 'Discover Summer' All-Ages Reading & Activity Programming
events.time: During branch open hours (varies by location)
events.description: Discover Summer is DCPL's all-ages, city-wide celebration of reading and learning, running June 1–August 31, 2026. Participating branches host drop-in reading programs, scavenger hunts (Beach Scavenger Hunt and America 250 Scavenger Hunt with prizes), storytimes, and other family-friendly activities through the end of August. Check individual branch pages for weekend hours.

events.title: DC JazzFest at The Wharf
events.venue: The Wharf (multiple stages: Arena Stage, Union Stage, Pearl Street Warehouse, outdoor piers)
events.description: The signature outdoor jazz festival weekend at The Wharf, featuring Grammy Award winners and NEA Jazz Masters including Dee Dee Bridgewater, Kurt Elling & the Yellowjackets, Joshua Redman, Cory Henry & The Funk Apostles, Nate Smith, and Emmet Cohen. Multi-day and single-day tickets available; family-friendly with a kids' scavenger hunt.

events.title: DC JazzFest at The Wharf & Southwest venues
events.venue: District Pier / Union Stage / Pearl Street Warehouse / Arena Stage, The Wharf
events.price: Free general admission; VIP/Preferred Seating ticketed
events.description: The signature weekend of DC JazzFest 2026 (Sept. 2–6), themed 'The Future of Jazz: America's Next 250 Years.' Saturday and Sunday action moves to The Wharf's District Pier, Union Stage, and Pearl Street Warehouse, with performances from 2–10 PM. Lineup includes Emmet Cohen's Miles & Trane tribute, Dee Dee Bridgewater Quartet, Joshua Redman Quartet, Cory Henry & The Funk Apostles, Bill Frisell Trio, Danilo Pérez Trio, and more. Part of America's 250th anniversary programming.

events.title: Eastern Market
events.description: Historic public market on Capitol Hill with local farmers, artisans, and crafters. The weekend flea and farmers market runs year-round and is a beloved neighborhood anchor.

events.title: Gruesome Playground Injuries – Keegan Theatre
events.description: A witty dark comedy about playground memories and romance at Keegan Theatre. Two connected souls find each other across time in a play that mixes dark wit with tender humor. Running August 15 through September 6.

events.title: Half Street Central Farmers Market
events.description: A vibrant outdoor market in Navy Yard featuring over 30 local vendors with fresh produce, baked goods, prepared foods, and artisanal products. Held every Saturday from spring through fall, with live music, chef demos, and family-friendly activities just steps from Nationals Park.

events.title: Smithsonian Castle – 'American Aspirations' Exhibition
events.description: The recently reopened Smithsonian Castle on the National Mall hosts 'American Aspirations,' an exhibition inviting visitors to consider how the founding ideals of 1776 have been interpreted across generations. Additional first-floor areas open through September 7, 2026. Free entry.

events.title: Smithsonian National Museum of American History – 'In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness' Exhibition
events.description: The Smithsonian's National Museum of American History is leading America's 250th-anniversary celebrations with 'In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness,' a bold immersive exhibition tracing how Americans have pursued the promises of the nation's founding. DC Public Library has a partner table for fun activities, suggested reading lists, and library swag. Completely free; no tickets required for general admission. Note: museum access may be modified on Aug 21–23 due to Freedom 250 Grand Prix.

events.title: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History – Free General Admission & Ongoing Exhibits
events.description: The Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History is always free. Across all three target weekends, families can explore permanent collections and current exhibits. Includes Q?rius, The Coralyn W. Whitney Science Education Center on the ground floor — a hands-on science lab open to teens and adults. Note: museum access may be modified on Aug 21–23 due to the Freedom 250 Grand Prix; plan ahead at si.edu.

events.title: US Botanic Garden – 'America's State Flowers: An America250 Celebration' & 'Fierce Flora' Exhibits
events.time: Regular garden hours (10:00 AM – 5:00 PM daily)
events.description: The US Botanic Garden Conservatory is free and open daily. Across all three target weekends, visitors can explore 'America's State Flowers: An America250 Celebration,' a garden-wide exhibit featuring flowers chosen by all U.S. states and territories, plus the new 'Fierce Flora: Tales of Survival and Demise' exhibit about unusual plant survival features. No tickets required.

events.title: Capitol Riverfront Friday Night Concert Series – Yards Park
events.description: Free Friday night concert series on the Yards Park boardwalk along the Anacostia River, running through September 11. Family-friendly with grassy open space, river views, food and beverages available for purchase. Specific artist TBA for Aug 28; series wraps Sept 11.

events.title: Eastern Market Saturday Outdoor Market
events.description: Eastern Market's weekly Saturday outdoor market runs along 7th Street SE from Pennsylvania Ave SE to North Carolina Ave SE, featuring farmers, artists, crafters, and prepared food sellers. Live music from local bands adds to the atmosphere on weekends.

events.title: The Wharf Farmers Market (Saturday)
events.description: Weekly Saturday farmers market at M Street Landing at The Wharf, supporting local farmers offering locally sourced food along the waterfront. Running since April 2026 through the season.

events.title: Eastern Market Sunday Outdoor Market
events.description: Eastern Market's weekly Sunday outdoor market featuring local farmers, artists, crafters, and prepared food sellers. Running June through September, this is a beloved Capitol Hill community tradition.

events.title: Venus
events.price: Single tickets TBA; Woolly Mammoth offers pay-what-you-can (PWYC) and $20-under-30 pricing
events.description: A world-premiere rolling world premiere by Steve Yockey, directed by new Artistic Director Reggie D. White. Follows orderly Nicole and instinctive Beth — two complete opposites whose love spirals into a darkly comedic tale of fear and obsession. Plays the weekends of Sep 12–13 and Sep 19–20.

events.title: Capitol Riverfront Friday Night Concert Series (14th Season) – Aug 15
events.venue: Yards Park Boardwalk, 355 Water St SE
events.description: The free Capitol Riverfront Friday Night Concert Series returns for its 14th season at the Yards Park boardwalk. Local bands play on the waterfront while families spread out on the grass; the park's water features double as a splash pad for kids. Food and drinks available on site.

events.title: DC Improv Stand-Up Showcase (Dom Grayer, Liam Nelson, Dom Hatton-Woods, Ty Colgate)
events.description: Weekend stand-up showcase featuring Dom Grayer, Liam Nelson, Dom Hatton-Woods, and Ty Colgate. Multiple shows Friday through Sunday. 18+ venue with a 2-item food/beverage minimum per customer.

events.title: Found Footage Fest: Porcelain VHS Treasures – Live Comedy with VHS Tapes
events.description: Brand new 2026 show from Found Footage Fest — live comedy built around curated VHS tape clips. Hilarious and interactive event at the Arlington Drafthouse dine-in theater. 21+ unless accompanied by a parent.

events.title: Show at 9:30 Club (Rock – Sat Aug 15)

events.title: WIT Harold Night

events.description: WIT's weekly Harold Night — a homage to the world-famous longform improv format. An audience suggestion sparks unique worlds filled with vibrant characters, created on the spot. Three show slots at 7:30, 8:30, and 9:30 PM on Monday Aug 17 (overlapping the Aug 15–16 weekend). All-ages improv comedy.

events.title: Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington DC
events.description: The first-ever NTT INDYCAR Series race on the National Mall, celebrating America's 250th anniversary. The temporary street circuit weaves past the Washington Monument, the U.S. Capitol, and other iconic landmarks. Free two-day motorsports event; tickets must be requested in advance.

events.title: Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C.
events.description: The first-ever NTT INDYCAR SERIES race on the National Mall, held across August 22–23 to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. World-class racing set against the backdrop of the Washington Monument and U.S. Capitol. Free tickets can be requested via the event website. Note: visitor access to some nearby Smithsonian museums will be modified during these dates.

events.title: LaVar Walker – Stand-Up Comedy
events.description: LaVar Walker, American stand-up comedian, writer, and pharmacist who has appeared on television and toured nationally, performs at Arlington Cinema & Drafthouse. Dine-in experience with in-seat food and drinks. 21+ unless accompanied by a parent.

events.title: Library of Congress National Book Festival 2026
events.description: The 26th annual Library of Congress National Book Festival fills the Convention Center with author conversations, readings, book signings, family activities, Young Adult and Middle Grade stages, workshops, and interactive exhibits. Part of the America 250: It's Your Story initiative. Free tickets must be reserved in advance at loc.gov/bookfest.

events.title: Masego: Fix Your Face Tour

events.title: National Book Festival

Book signings, readings, and programming for all ages. Registration recommended.

events.title: Show at 9:30 Club (Sat Aug 22)

events.title: WABA × BPAC: Celebrate Holland Lane Bike Lanes & End-of-Summer Social

Hosted by WABA in partnership with the Alexandria Bicycle & Pedestrian Advisory Committee (BPAC). Short, easy ride celebrating the completion of a protected bike lane project.

events.title: Washington Folk Festival

events.title: WABA Red Line Corridor Guided Group Ride

events.description: WABA-guided group ride along the Red Line construction corridor every Monday through August 31. The route starts at North Bethesda Metro and follows the Trolley Trail and Capital Crescent Trail, stopping at Medical Center and Bethesda stations before ending at Friendship Heights — a practical and scenic alternative while Metro buses replace trains during the summer shutdown.

events.title: Sunset Cinema at The Wharf – Project Hail Mary

The 'America's State Flowers: An America250 Celebration' exhibit is on view garden-wide. No tickets required.

events.description: WABA returns to Hains Point for a second community ride and advocacy event, making noise to keep Hains Point open and accessible to all. A celebratory community ride at one of DC's most beloved multiuse public spaces as it faces ongoing federal threats.
